documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Time of eval: 23:40, ED bay 4
Chief complaint: cough and fever x 4 days, worsening shortness of breath today
HPI:
55 yo female, prior good health, presents with 4 days of productive cough, rust-colored sputum, subjective fevers to 39 at home.
Progressive dyspnea over 48h, now short of breath walking across room. Right-sided pleuritic chest pain with deep breath and cough.
Two episodes of emesis today after attempting fluids; poor oral intake since yesterday. No diarrhea.
No hemoptysis, no leg swelling, no calf pain. No recent travel. No sick contacts known. No TB exposure.
Denies headache, neck stiffness, rash. Fully alert and answering all questions appropriately throughout eval.
PMH: HTN, prediabetes, GERD, remote appendectomy.
Home meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, MVI. No inhalers.
Allergies: sulfa - rash.
Social: former smoker, 8 pack-years, quit ~12 yrs ago. Rare alcohol. No IVDU. Lives with husband and adult daughter.
FH: father CAD, mother DM2.
ROS:
Constitutional: fevers, chills, myalgias, fatigue.
Resp: cough, dyspnea, pleuritic pain. No wheeze at baseline.
CV: no orthopnea, no PND, no syncope.
GI: nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite. No abdominal pain.
GU: no dysuria. Remainder of 10-system ROS negative.
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Triage vitals: T 38.9, HR 112, BP 124/72, respiratory rate 32 at triage, SpO2 93% on RA.
Repeat at 4 hours: T 38.4, HR 104, BP 118/70, respiratory rate 30 at 4 hours, SpO2 93% RA.
Gen: ill-appearing, diaphoretic, speaking in short sentences.
HEENT: MMM slightly dry, oropharynx clear, no JVD.
Lungs: decreased breath sounds and coarse crackles right base and right mid-axillary line, dullness to percussion right base, egophony present. Left field clear.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no rub.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema, no cyanosis. Cap refill brisk.
Neuro: alert, follows all commands, moves all extremities, no focal deficit.
Skin: warm, no rash.
LABS:
WBC 17.8 with 88% neutrophils, bands 9%. Hgb 13.2, Plt 288.
Na 133, K 3.6, Cl 98, HCO3 22, BUN 16, Cr 0.9, glucose 138.
Lactate 2.3. AST 34, ALT 28, T bili 0.8. CRP 186. Procalcitonin 4.2.
Blood cultures x2 drawn 23:05. Sputum gram stain and culture sent. Resp viral panel pending. Urine pneumococcal and legionella antigens sent.
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Effusion too small to tap.
ASSESSMENT:
55 yo F with community-acquired pneumonia, right lower and right middle lobe, with small right pleural effusion.
CURB-65 of 1, scored for age only - no uremia, normal mentation, BP adequate. Admitting to medical floor rather than ICU given hypoxia is mild but RR elevated and pt cannot keep fluids down.
Vomiting precludes oral therapy at present; will use IV route.
PLAN:
1. CAP: ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin 500 mg daily. Unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting, so no PO abx for now.
2. Hypoxia: maintain SpO2 >92%. Continuous pulse ox overnight, supplemental O2 PRN via NC.
3. Vomiting/volume: NS 1L bolus then 100 mL/hr x 6h. Ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h PRN. Hold PO except sips.
4. Tachypnea/work of breathing: RT to assess, incentive spirometer q1h while awake.
5. Effusion: follow clinically, repeat imaging if worsening or new fever spike.
6. Hold lisinopril while volume depleted. Continue PPI IV.
7. Pain: acetaminophen 650 mg IV q6h PRN, avoid NSAIDs for now.
8. VTE ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.
9. Trend lactate, CBC, BMP in AM.
Discussed with pt and daughter at bedside; questions answered. Attending notified 23:55.
Disposition: telemetry floor, O2 sat monitoring.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:30
Subjective: Pt reports cough still productive, less pleuritic pain. Vomited twice overnight (01:20, 04:50) after sips of water. Denies chest pressure. Alert, oriented, conversant.
Overnight event: 1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping at 02:10. Sat rose to 96% on 1L. Weaned off while awake, 93-94% RA sitting up.
Vitals: T max 38.6 at 03:00, now 37.8. HR 96. BP 116/68. RR 24. SpO2 94% RA at rest.
I/O: in 2100 mL IV, out 1450 mL. Weight up 0.8 kg.
Exam: less diaphoretic. Lungs - crackles right base and right mid field, dullness right base unchanged. Cardiac regular. Abd soft. No edema.
Labs HD2: WBC 15.1 (from 17.8), Hgb 12.8, Plt 301. Na 135, K 3.8, Cr 0.8, HCO3 23. Lactate 1.3.
Blood cultures: no growth at 12h. Resp viral panel negative. Legionella urine antigen negative. Sputum culture pending, gram stain gram-positive diplococci.
Assessment: CAP with right lower/right middle lobe infiltrate and small right pleural effusion, day 2 of therapy. Early clinical response - defervescing, WBC down, lactate cleared.
Persistent vomiting limits oral therapy. Continuing IV route.
Plan:
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. Unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiging through day 2 - reassess PO trial this afternoon.
2. O2: keep 1L NC at night if sats drop below 92% asleep; wean to RA when awake. Continuous pulse ox tonight.
3. Antiemetics: switch to ondansetron 4 mg IV scheduled q8h x 24h. Add small clear liquid trial at 14:00.
4. IVF 75 mL/hr, reassess with morning labs.
5. Incentive spirometer q1h awake, OOB to chair with RN assist, ambulate in hall this afternoon.
6. Effusion small - no drainage indicated. Repeat CXR only if clinical worsening.
7. Continue holding lisinopril. Continue enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.
8. Follow sputum and blood culture results, narrow abx when speciated.
Discussed plan with pt; husband at bedside. RT and RN updated.
Time spent: 25 min.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD4, 08:05
Subjective: Marked improvement. No vomiting since HD2 evening. Ate most of breakfast. Cough looser, minimal sputum. Walked hall x2 yesterday with RN, mild dyspnea only at end.
Vitals: afebrile x 36h, T max 37.3. HR 78. BP 122/74. RR 18. SpO2 95% on RA ambulating, 97% RA at rest.
Off supplemental O2 since HD3 05:00 including overnight; no desats recorded on continuous pulse ox.

Exam: comfortable, no accessory muscle use, speaking full sentences. Lungs - scattered crackles right base only, mid field clear, dullness less prominent. CV regular. Abd soft, bowel sounds normal. No edema. Alert and fully conversant.
Labs HD4: WBC 9.2, Hgb 12.6, Plt 340. Na 138, K 4.0, BUN 11, Cr 0.8. CRP 62 (down from 186).
Micro: blood cultures x2 no growth at 72h - final. Sputum culture S. pneumoniae, pan-sensitive including penicillin.
Assessment: CAP, right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion, pneumococcal by sputum. Day 4 - clinical resolution, tolerating PO, oxygenating on room air.
Plan:
1. Transition antibiotics to oral amoxicillin today given pan-sensitive pneumococcus and resolved vomiting; discontinue IV azithromycin. Total course 5 days.
2. Observe tolerance of first two PO doses; if tolerated, plan discharge HD5.
3. O2: remains off, keep spot checks q shift. No overnight O2 needed.
4. Discontinue IV fluids. Encourage oral hydration, goal 1.5 L/day.
5. Restart lisinopril 10 mg daily today - Cr normal, BP adequate.
6. Discontinue scheduled ondansetron, keep PRN.
7. Continue incentive spirometer, ambulate TID.
8. Effusion small and resolving clinically - no repeat imaging inpatient. Outpatient CXR in 6 weeks to confirm resolution given smoking history.
9. Continue enoxaparin until ambulating independently.
10. Begin discharge teaching: abx completion, return precautions, smoking-free maintenance, pneumococcal and influenza vaccination at follow-up.
Pt and daughter updated at bedside, agreeable. Attending saw pt 08:40, agrees with plan.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD5
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: HD1 via ED. Discharge: HD5, 11:20. Length of stay 5 days.
Discharge diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower and right middle lobe, with small right pleural effusion; Streptococcus pneumoniae by sputum culture.
Secondary: HTN, prediabetes, GERD, former smoker.
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
55 yo F presented with 4 days of fever, productive cough and progressive dyspnea with right pleuritic pain.
At triage: T 38.9, HR 112, respiratory rate 32 at triage, and respiratory rate 30 at 4 hours; SpO2 93% on RA. WBC 17.8, lactate 2.3.
Chest x-ray showed right lower and right middle lobe infiltrate with small right pleural effusion. CURB-65 of 1, scored for age only; admitted to medical floor.
Started on ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and IV azithromycin. Unable to tolerate oral intake due to vomiting through day 2, so antibiotics and fluids given IV.
1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping on HD1-2; weaned to room air HD3 and remained off oxygen thereafter, including overnight.
Vomiting resolved HD2 evening with scheduled ondansetron. Diet advanced HD3.
Afebrile from HD3. WBC 17.8 to 9.2, CRP 186 to 62. Lactate cleared to 1.3.
Blood cultures x2 no growth, final. Sputum culture S. pneumoniae, pan-sensitive. Legionella urine antigen and respiratory viral panel negative.
Narrowed to oral amoxicillin HD4; tolerated without nausea. Effusion small, never required drainage.
Ambulating in hall independently on HD5, SpO2 95-97% on RA with ambulation. Discharged home in stable condition.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.9, HR 76, BP 118/72, RR 16, SpO2 96% RA.
DISCHARGE EXAM: comfortable, no distress. Few fine crackles right base. Alert, fully conversant. No edema.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Amoxicillin 1 g PO TID x 2 more days to complete 5-day total course.
2. Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily - resumed HD4.
3. Omeprazole 20 mg PO daily.
4. Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain or fever.
5. Ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h PRN nausea, #10.
6. Multivitamin daily.
Enoxaparin discontinued at discharge.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 7-10 days for symptom recheck and vaccination review (pneumococcal, influenza).
Chest x-ray in 6 weeks to document resolution of infiltrate and effusion, given prior smoking history.
RETURN PRECAUTIONS: return or call for fever above 38.3, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, inability to keep fluids down, or lightheadedness.
INSTRUCTIONS: complete all antibiotic doses, use incentive spirometer 10x hourly while awake for 1 week, walk daily, drink 1.5-2 L fluids, remain smoke-free.
Discharge teaching completed with pt and daughter; both verbalized understanding. Pending labs at discharge: none.
